title: Display: Flex
summary: Opens the Flexbox section with a history of page-layout techniques (tables, inline-block, absolute positioning, floats) and why flexbox replaced them. Shows that display: flex on a container lays children in a row, introduces gap and inline-flex, then has the learner turn a list into a horizontal nav bar.

concepts.heading: Layout methods that came before flexbox
points: HTML tables (table, tr, td) with set column widths can build a multi-column layout, but table markup should only be used for real tabular data, never for page layout.
display: inline-block with explicit widths puts boxes on one line, but vertical alignment is awkward and elements collapse down when space runs out, so it is fiddly to control.

position: absolute pulls boxes out of normal flow and offsets them (for example with left); it works but is inflexible: anything added later forces re-adjustment and it does not respond to screen size.
float (popular circa 2005-2010) can make columns by floating items left or right and clearing a footer; it needed workarounds such as the clearfix hack and is hard to reason about and debug.
Takeaway: keep float for its original job (wrapping text around an image) and use flexbox, grid or a framework for page structure. Floats can still be used inside individual blocks.

concepts.heading: display: flex basics
points: Wrap the elements in a container element and set display: flex on the container (the parent), not on the children.
The direct children become flex items and line up in a row, each normally sized by its content, regardless of whether they were block or inline elements before.

Flexbox is a separate layout system: the usual display rules (div is block, span is inline, etc.) no longer apply to the items; flexbox rules take over. The container itself behaves like a block (full available width).
gap sets spacing between items. A fixed value such as 10px is static; a rem value such as 1rem scales with the root font size.

display: inline-flex makes the container itself behave inline (only as wide as needed, other content can share its line), mirroring the block / inline-block distinction. The items inside behave the same either way.
Many more properties (axes, direction, alignment, wrapping) are covered in later lessons; the next lesson covers the flex axis and direction.

concepts.heading: Demo files that come with the exercise
points: index.html links to demo pages: html-table.html, inline-block.html, absolute-position.html, float.html and flex.html, each producing a three-column layout so you can compare the code needed. flex.html needs only a few lines.
(Extra) In the reference repo the three-column flex demo is just .container { display: flex; gap: 10px; } with the columns as divs inside.

concepts.heading: Challenge walkthrough
points: Starting page: a div.container holding a paragraph title and several li links, with list-style: none already removing the bullets, so everything stacks vertically.
Fix: in the .container rule change display to flex, which puts all items on one line like a nav bar.
Add a gap (for example 10px or 1rem) so the links are not touching.
The solution therefore only adds two declarations: display: flex and gap.

code_examples.caption: Flex container with gap
Challenge solution: list items become a horizontal nav bar

task.name: Turn a list into a horizontal nav bar with flexbox
task.starting_point: index.html with a div.container containing a title paragraph and five li links (list-style none already applied); items stack vertically. A goal image shows the target.
task.goal: Display all items on one horizontal line with a gap between them, using flexbox.
steps: Open index.html in preview and compare with goal.png.
In the .container rule set display: flex.
Add a gap (10px or a rem value) to space the items.
Toggle list-style to see what it does, then check solution.html.
task.expected_result: Title and links sit in a single gold row separated by even gaps.

pitfalls: Setting display: flex on the items instead of the container.
Expecting old block/inline rules to still apply to flex items.
Using HTML tables or floats for page layout.
The reference repo has an author footer ('Made with ... by ...') that is not part of the course; its index.html also already contains the finished flex solution.

playground.coverage: Covers display: flex and gap on a container and adds a flex-basis step. Explore demo is a full flexbox property playground with a main/cross axis readout.
gaps_and_ideas: Add the history: show the same three-column layout built with table, inline-block, absolute and float next to the flex version.
Add the nav-bar challenge from the course (list of links to a horizontal bar) as a second task, since the playground uses numbered boxes instead.
Add a display: flex vs inline-flex toggle in the explore demo, with a visible border around the container to show full-width vs shrink-wrapped.
Add a gap unit comparison (10px vs 1rem, changing root font size).
Note that flex ignores items' previous block/inline display, e.g. mix a span and a div as children.
